newsitem.title: FRANCE: TF1 market share down but audience stable - head.
newsitem.headline: TF1 market share down but audience stable - head.

text.p: Market share at French private television channel TF1 has dipped over recent years as the market itself grew, but overall its audience has remained stable, said Corinne Bougyues, chairman of TF1 Publicite, the station's advertising subsidiary.
She told advertising industry weekly newspaper Strategies, published on Friday, that talk of a slide in TF1's market share was overdone.
"Take housewives under 50, between 1989 and 1996 TF1 has lost 2.6 points in market share. It's not that much, when you take into account the number of new channels," she said in an interview.
"TF1's market share has fallen slightly on advertising targets, just because the market has grown, but its audience has been maintained," she said.

She said it was not easy to put a figure on how much the channel could benefit from a decision by France's broadcasting watchdog, the Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA), to allow advertising breaks of six minutes rather than four minutes half way through films.
In France, channels can only put one advertising break in the middle of films screened on television.
